A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 18-page versions of Astra, including Appendices A-E. Their corresponding text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Astra-Bench evaluations and ablations in Tables 2-3, plus action-alignment measurements, CityWalker evaluation, out-of-domain examples and history-length analysis in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, component ablations and supplementary evaluations in Appendices A-D.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.3 retain the same autoregressive denoising framework, ACT-Adapter, action-free guidance, noisy history memory and mixture of action experts.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes, Sekai, SpatialVID, RT-1 and Multi-Cam Video, and retain the CityWalker evaluation and indoor, Minecraft and animation out-of-domain scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and D retain Wan-2.1, MatrixGame and YUME. Appendix Table A and Figure B retain Navigation World Models, labeled NWM/NVM. Comparator membership is unchanged within each comparison.

E3.justification: Both retain the same training budget, metrics, 20 held-out samples per training dataset, 100 CityWalker scenes, 20 human evaluators and generation settings. Removing the H800 designation reduces hardware specificity without establishing a change in the experimental setup.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same guidance, noise, adapter and MoAE ablations. The parameter analysis, out-of-domain examples and history-length analysis in Appendices A.5, C.2 and D are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain Table 3's statement that ablations use the same random seed. Neither version reports additional repeated-run information, uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and qualitative result panels are unchanged. For example, Astra's instruction-following scores remain 0.669 in Table 2 and 0.641 in Table D, while Table A retains rotation and translation errors of 1.23 and 4.86.

T1.justification: Equations 1-4 and the conditioning, flow-matching and expert-routing formulations are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about general interactive world modeling, action responsiveness, long-term consistency and support for heterogeneous action modalities.

C2.justification: The visual-inertia explanation, MoAE tradeoffs and generalization interpretations are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same inference-efficiency and real-time deployment limitations.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.2 replace eight H800 GPUs with eight unspecified GPUs, retaining 80 GB memory per GPU. This removes hardware-model information; hyperparameters, the approximately 24-hour training time and project/code access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography and positioning against existing world models are unchanged. No cited works or substantive novelty comparisons are added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 adds equal-contribution markers for Yixuan Zhu and Jiaqi Feng and the corresponding footnote, updates the arXiv version/date stamp and lightly edits the training-hardware wording. Section organization and the scientific narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The equal-contribution note lengthens the title-page footnote and its rule, while revised training wording changes local line wrapping. All figures, tables, captions and their placements are preserved.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies equal authorship but removes the H800 hardware designation from both training descriptions while retaining the approximately 24-hour convergence claim. With the scientific content and evidence unchanged, this loss of hardware specificity modestly reduces reproducibility and the interpretability of training cost.
